examples: food stuck in throat can't breathe
choking on a piece of meat
he can't breathe something is stuck in his throat
choking_adult.answer: 1. Encourage them to cough. 2. If coughing does not clear it, give up to five back blows between the shoulder blades. 3. If that fails, give up to five abdominal thrusts. 4. Call 999 if the blockage does not clear. Alternate five back blows and five abdominal thrusts until help arrives.

examples: he is not breathing and unconscious
my dad collapsed and isn't breathing
cardiac_arrest.answer: 1. Call 999 immediately and ask for an ambulance. 2. Start CPR: push hard and fast in the centre of the chest at 100 to 120 compressions per minute. 3. If an AED is available, switch it on and follow its instructions. 4. Do not stop until professional help takes over.

examples: lots of blood from a cut
bleeding badly with glass in the wound
heavy bleeding what do I do
severe_bleeding.answer: 1. Call 999. 2. Apply firm direct pressure to the wound with a clean cloth. 3. If an object is embedded, do not remove it; apply pressure around it. 4. Keep pressure on until emergency services arrive. Lie the person down and reassure them.

examples: chest pain and pain down left arm
he might be having a heart attack
heart_attack.answer: 1. Call 999 immediately. 2. Help them sit down and rest. 3. If available and they are not allergic, help them chew a 300 mg aspirin. 4. Stay with them and monitor their breathing until the ambulance arrives.

examples: spilled boiling water on my hand
burnt my arm on the oven
burnt my hand what do I do
burn.answer: 1. Cool the burn under cool running water for at least 20 minutes. 2. Remove jewellery or clothing near the burn unless stuck to the skin. 3. Do not apply creams, butter, or ice. 4. Cover loosely with cling film. Seek medical help for large or deep burns.

examples: allergic reaction face swelling can't breathe
bee sting swelling and trouble breathing
she is having an allergic reaction and struggling to breathe
anaphylaxis.answer: 1. This is a medical emergency, call 999 immediately. 2. If they have an adrenaline auto-injector (EpiPen), help them use it without delay. 3. Help them lie down with legs raised, or sit up if breathing is difficult. 4. A second dose may be given after five minutes if needed and available.

examples: person shaking on the floor convulsing
having a fit on the ground
seizure.answer: 1. Move nearby objects away to protect them from injury. 2. Do not restrain them and do not put anything in their mouth. 3. Cushion their head. 4. Time the seizure. Call 999 if it lasts longer than five minutes or another follows.

minor_cut.answer: 1. Wash the cut under running water. 2. Apply gentle pressure with a clean cloth to stop the bleeding. 3. Cover with a plaster or dressing. Seek medical advice if it is deep or does not stop bleeding.
